# dsh-web-search-searxng

A SearXNG-backed `WebSearchProvider` for the DeepSeek Harness web
capability seam (`ctx.web`).

It registers a provider with the id `searxng` and adds no tool of its own: `web_search` is already
r

egistered by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-web`, and this package only gives it a backend that needs no
thi

epseek-ai/dsh-tool-web`, and this package only gives it a backend that needs no
third-party API key.
## Why this exists
The default provider (`deepseek-official`) authenticates in one of two ways:

1. a DeepSeek **account sign-in**, used only when the session's model request is served by the
`deep

seek-account` provider route;
2. a `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`.

When models are served through a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible gateway, (1) never applies and (2)
ma

y not be configured, so every search fails with `WEB_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_MISSING`. Pointing the
same
`web_search` tool at a local SearXNG instance removes that dependency entirely.
## Requirements
- A running SearXNG instance with the **JSON output format enabled** — it is off by default:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- Node's built-in `fetch` (Node.js >= 18). No runtime dependencies.

## Configuration
| Key | Default | Description |

| `baseURL` | `http://127.0.0.1:8888` | SearXNG origin; a trailing slash is tolerated |
| `language`

| — | Forwarded as SearXNG's `language` (e.g. `zh-CN`); omit for the default `all` |
| `safesearch`

| `0` | `0` off, `1` moderate, `2` strict |
| `timeoutMs` | `20000` | Per-request budget |
## Failure behaviour
| Situation | Result |

| Instance unreachable | Throws with the origin and a `docker ps` / `colima start` hint |
| Non-2xx

response | Throws with the status code and origin |
| `200` with zero results **and** failing engine

s | Throws, including `unresponsive_engines` |
| `200` with zero results and no engine errors | Retu
rns an empty `sources` array — a genuine miss |

The third row is deliberate. SearXNG reports "no matching results" and "every engine failed" with
th
e same `200`/empty payload, so a passthrough makes a broken deployment look like a quiet miss.
## Engine selection and rate limits

SearXNG is a metasearch front end: most engines ship disabled, and which ones answer depends on
your

network. Two engines are not enough. When Brave or Google throttles you, SearXNG suspends that
engi

ne for about 180 seconds (CAPTCHA blocks last far longer), and with no surviving engine the
search r
eturns nothing at all.
Keep at least two independent upstreams enabled, for example:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Measure instead of guessing — this lists the engines that failed on one query:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The provider reports throttling as such rather than as a deployment fault: when every result is
empt

y and the failing engines mention rate limits, the error says SearXNG retries the engine after a
~18

0s cooldown while the upstream quota can take considerably longer — so retrying immediately tends
to
fail again, and the useful responses are waiting or enabling a fallback engine.
## Example instance

`examples/searxng/` contains a minimal `docker-compose.yml` and `settings.yml` (JSON enabled,
limite

r off). Copy them, set a `secret_key`, adjust the outbound proxy if your network needs one,
then `do
cker compose up -d`.
## Uninstall
Remove the `insert` entry and point `web.searchProvider` back at the provider you want. The package
can stay installed; nothing else references it.
